comparison: Perfect agreement on mammalian cell validation (C45-C53, C57). Both evaluations support the cross-species conservation of DegV1 function. OpenEval provides more detailed analysis of kinetics and mechanistic controls, while peer reviewers accept the findings without challenge.

Both address mechanistic speculation about retrotranslocation (C64-C65) and rate as UNCERTAIN. OpenEval notes the data cannot distinguish between possibilities and suggests additional experiments. Peer reviewers highlight conceptual tension with N-terminal requirement and note mechanistic questions remain unresolved.

Strong overlap on library design and screening methodology (C20-C27, C67-C71). Both support the technical soundness of the approach. OpenEval provides detailed analysis of enrichment calculations and oversampling, while peer reviewers accept the methodology without criticism.

Both address ERAD mechanism characterization (C33-C38). Both evaluations are SUPPORTED. OpenEval emphasizes the thoroughness of proteasome inhibitor and genetic deletion experiments, while peer reviewers confirm the Hrd1 pathway involvement is demonstrated.

Both address position-dependence of degron activity (C29-C32) and rate as SUPPORTED. OpenEval notes the C-terminal test complication with HDEL signal, while peer reviewers explicitly accept that degrons only function at N-terminus without expressing concerns.

Both address application to endogenous proteins with different topologies (C39-C44, C54-C55). Both are SUPPORTED. OpenEval suggests quantitative half-life measurements would strengthen the work, while peer reviewers accept the diversity of protein types tested without requesting additional data.

Both address background/contextual claims about ERAD and degrons (C7-C9, C12, C14-C19, C62-C63). Both rate as SUPPORTED. These establish the field context and novelty basis. OpenEval notes appropriate citations; peer reviewers use these as premise for understanding novelty.

Both address bioinformatic analysis showing DegV1 absence from yeast genomes (C58-C59). OpenEval rates SUPPORTED for the technical finding but notes broader consensus not addressed. Peer reviewers rate UNCERTAIN, questioning physiological relevance and in vivo role of artificial sequences.

OpenEval addresses comparison to known ERAD substrates and degradation kinetics (C60-C61) as SUPPORTED. Peer R7 addresses related bioinformatic claims (C58-C59) as UNCERTAIN due to physiological relevance concerns. Partial overlap in addressing whether DegV1 represents physiologically relevant ERAD substrate behavior.

Both address background claims (C1-C3, C10-C11, C13) establishing prior state of field. Both rate as SUPPORTED. OpenEval emphasizes these establish novelty of ER luminal degrons; peer reviewers accept these as basis for understanding the work's contribution.

OpenEval R6 addresses summary claims about DegV1 versatility (C54-C56). Peer R5 addresses endogenous protein applications (C39-C44, C54-C55). Both SUPPORTED with partial overlap on C54-C55. OpenEval emphasizes breadth of validation; peer reviewers accept diverse protein targeting.

Minimal overlap on signal sequence cleavage control (C28). Both SUPPORTED. OpenEval notes this addresses important control for degron function mechanism. Peer reviewers accept this technical detail without challenge as supporting data quality.

OpenEval R12 addresses overall novelty claim (C66) as SUPPORTED with noted limitations. Peer R1 addresses core finding (C4-C6, C27, C66) as SUPPORTED, with editor and reviewers confirming this is 'important study' with 'solid evidence.' Both agree on fundamental contribution.

Limited overlap on library design context (C4) and functional validation (C27). OpenEval R1 focuses on technical details of screening methodology. Peer R1 focuses on overall acceptance of core finding. Both SUPPORTED but address different aspects of the work.

Minimal overlap on versatility claim (C56). OpenEval R6 addresses summary claims about DegV1 working with folded proteins and diverse substrates. Peer R4 addresses ERAD mechanism. Both SUPPORTED but focus on different experimental aspects.
